title: router.rs:721 direct-child anti-spoof gate silently dead post-migration
description: Discovered from the lost project-LICHEN-worker6-i72x.2 (worker8). rust/lichen-node/src/routing/router.rs:718-724: the DAO direct-child check 'parents.any(|p| same_interface(p, &self.dodag_id)) && !same_interface(&authenticated_sender, &packet_source) => reject' compares advertised DAO parents against the DODAG ID (root's routable /128) by low-half (same_interface = a[8..]==b[8..]). Production DAOs name parents in link-local form (see sibling bead on the two parent forms), so the first condition never fires post-migration and the relay-spoofing rejection is silently dead. No test covers it (all DAO tests pass target==authenticated_sender). The node.rs sibling gate (:604) was fixed in the i72x.2 rollup by matching BOTH own forms (link-local IID half + exact routable via dao_manager.node_address()); the router.rs gate cannot do that for the ROOT's identity - the node has no key->IID binding for the root. Needs the same design decision as the parent-forms bead: likely the DODAG should learn the root's link-local binding at authenticated DIO acceptance (frame.sender().pubkey -> routable == dodag_id -> remember root IID). C parity audit needed.
